options.text: Net exports rose from $450 billion to $560 billion, which increased aggregate demand.
options.why: These values are exports; net exports also subtract imports.

options.text: Net exports rose from -$10 billion to $40 billion, which decreased aggregate demand, because higher exports raise the price level.
options.why: Higher net exports add to aggregate demand; the price level effect does not reverse that.

options.text: Net exports fell from -$10 billion to $40 billion, which decreased aggregate demand.
options.why: Exports grew faster than imports, so net exports rose rather than fell.

options.text: Net exports rose from -$10 billion to $40 billion, which increased aggregate demand.
options.why: Net exports are exports minus imports; exports rose by more than imports, so net exports and aggregate demand rose.

options.text: Net exports did not change, because both exports and imports rose.
options.why: Net exports change when exports and imports rise by different amounts.

difficulty.label: basic_learning
difficulty.rationale: Student reads two curves at two points, computes net exports (X - M) for Year 2 (-10) and Year 5 (40), and links a rise in net exports to higher aggregate demand. Concept depth is shallow (NX is a component of AD), with one subtraction per year and one comparative-statics link. Distractors are clearly distinguishable (wrong level/direction, wrong mechanism, no-change). No exchange-rate shift is required, so the item sits at the foundational level rather than full-mock exam depth.

difficultyRationale: Student reads two points from a graph (Year 2 and Year 5), computes net exports twice with simple subtraction (-50 and -120), and links the fall in NX to a decrease in aggregate demand. Single concept (NX = X - M as an AD component), one comparative step, small whole-number arithmetic, low reading load. Distractors target common errors (ignoring imports, confusing level with change, sign confusion, imports raising AD). Fits recall/application level rather than full-mock multi-step difficulty. Note: no exchange-rate mechanism is involved, so it only partially exercises topic 6.5.
